attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, said in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithfully restates a general necessary-condition maxim. Calling it causal is fine, but as a universal methodological maxim it is effectively untestable.

contract.note: The contract rightly says that 'identify the problems' is undefined. Any test would depend on a meaning the speaker did not supply, so the not_applicable axis is fair.

evidence.note: Genuine 2020 scaling-laws abstract. It shows optimization guided by measured relationships, but it cannot test the maxim without a definition of identification.

reviews.rationale: This is a broad engineering maxim with no operational meaning for 'identifying problems'. Whether random search or scaling-law optimization counts as a counterexample depends entirely on an interpretation the speaker did not give, so the claim cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own self-assessment in his own post.

semantics.note: An observation that all seven of his March 2024 economic predictions had held as of 11 December 2024. Identifying the seven from his March list is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'modest profits' literally (some profit, but modest) is ordinary, not stretched, and the contract notes that losses fit his wider point. 'Massive advance', moat and adoption have no measure, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Third-party list of the seven predictions, dated before the evaluation date. Its verdict on o1 is opinion, and it reports his 7/7 self-rating.
May 2024 price cuts in China described as a price war. This supports the price-wars item.
October 2024 OpenAI admission that hallucinations remain an open problem. This supports the no-robust-fix item.
OpenAI expected about a $5B loss for 2024. Read literally, the leading developer had no 'modest profits'. The figure is an estimate, not a realized result.
OpenAI's own account of o1's benchmark gains. Whether this is a 'massive advance' is subjective, so it does not settle that item.

reviews.rationale: The price-wars and hallucination items held. The profits item did not hold on a literal reading: OpenAI expected a large loss. The no-massive-advance item is disputed because of o1, and the 7-10 models, moat and adoption items have no evidence. So the claim that all seven held is not established, although several parts hold.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his own post.

semantics.note: Two linked observations: no profit so far, and an internal expectation of no profit before 2029. It is correctly not treated as a forecast.

contract.note: Company-wide annual net profit is the ordinary reading. The contract fairly separates realized history from projections.

evidence.note: October 2024 report of a projected 2024 loss. It is a projection for one year, not a realized historical record.
Secondary summary of documents obtained by The Information, saying OpenAI projected no profit until 2029. This supports the expectations clause only.

reviews.rationale: Secondary reporting supports the clause that OpenAI did not expect a profit before 2029. No realized financial record in the packet establishes that OpenAI had never made a profit, and the evidence is projections. Nothing contradicts the claim, but the historical clause is unverified.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'by many measures' and 'reportedly'. 'Reportedly' attributes the claim to reports; it is not a probability hedge, so the claim is scored. Leaving out the jab at Newton is acceptable.

contract.note: The contract reads him as asserting a real slowdown, softened by reports. That is fair given his framing of a 'fundamental distinction'. A reports-only reading would be narrower.

evidence.note: November 2024 Reuters: Sutskever says pretraining gains have plateaued, and sources describe disappointing attempts to beat GPT-4. This supports that slowdown reports existed, but gives no multi-measure comparison.
TIME cites several slowdown reports alongside Anthropic's denial and calls the picture mixed. It does not settle the rate comparison.
OpenAI's own disclosure of large o1 reasoning gains. This is an isolated counterpoint from another method, not a comparison of rates.

reviews.rationale: Credible late-2024 reports of diminishing pretraining returns support the 'reportedly' part. The packet has no comparable multi-measure evidence for 2019-2022 against 2023-2024, and o1's gains plus Anthropic's denial complicate the picture. Neither the contract's support condition nor its contradiction condition is met.
